To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

behavioral interventions that target the risk factors of late-life depression (e.g., social isolation, sleep disturbances, cognitive impairments) can improve outcomes for older adults who are at risk for depression and who do not respond to selective serotonin re-uptake inhibitor medications; and, that behavioral interventions that target risk factors of depression can be personalized for individual patients by matching interventions with risk factors.
behavioral interventions can be personalized based on the causes of depression.

(a) late-life depression can be treated effectively using behavioral interventions that target the specific causes of depression in older adults; (b) behavioral interventions are more effective when they are tailored to the needs of the individual; (c) the process of tailoring a behavioral intervention to the needs of an individual can be accomplished by a team of researchers and clinicians; and (d) the same process can be applied to other psychiatric disorders.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a personalized treatment approach to depression.
the development of behavioral interventions that are tailored to specific subgroups of patients with depression.
the development of a personalized approach to behavioral treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the selection of behavioral intervention strategies should be informed by a thorough understanding of the causes of the disorder and the mechanisms of action of those interventions.
behavioral interventions can be personalized to the needs of patients with depression.
personalized behavioral interventions have great potential in depression treatment and should be considered in the future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are trying to create a research agenda that will lead to the development of behavioral interventions that can be used to improve the treatment of depression in older adults.

the use of a personalized treatment approach to the design and evaluation of behavioral interventions can help us to understand more about the causes of depression and to identify interventions that are effective for specific subgroups of patients.
we are developing an infrastructure to support the development of personalized behavioral interventions for late-life depression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
behavioral interventions are a promising component of personalized treatment.

behavioral interventions are not a one-size-fits-all approach to depression treatment, and that the selection of a particular intervention should be guided by a thorough understanding of the causes of depression in a particular individual.
behavioral interventions can be personalized by selecting those that address risk factors for poor response to medication.
